///\n536\t    /// ## Errors\n537\t    ///\n538\t    /// Returns an error if:\n539\t    /// - The test run fails\n540\t    /// - Output directory creation fails\n541\t    /// - File writing test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n553\t        // First run the test to get the outcome\n554\t        let outcome = self.run()?;\n555\t\n556\t        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n557\t        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n558\t            // Write stdout\n559\t            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n560\t                tracing::warn!(\n561\t                    test_name = %test_name,\n562\t                    error = %e,\n563\t                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n564\t                );\n565\t            }\n566\t\n567\t            // Write stderr\n568\t            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n569\t                tracing::warn!(\n570\t                    test_name = %test_name,\n571\t                    error = %e,\n572\t                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n573\t                );\n574\t            }\n575\t\n576\t         tracing::warn!(\n580\t                    test_name = %test_name,\n581\t                    error = %e,\n582\t                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n583\t                );\n584\t            }\n585\t\n586\t            tracing::info!(\n587\t                test_name = %test_name,\n588\t                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n589\t );\n593\t        } else {\n594\t            tracing::warn!(\n595\t                test_name = %test_name,\n596\t                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not /// ```\n630\t    pub fn run_with_bead_trace(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n631\t        // First run the test to get the outcome\n632\t        let outcome = self.run()?;\n633\t\n634\t        // Create bead trace directory and write outputs\n635\t        let bead_id = BeadId::from(bead_id);\n636\t        if let Some(trace) = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id,      Ok(outcome)\n670\t    }\n671\t}\n672\t\n673\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n674\t// Utility Functions\n675\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n676\t\n677\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n678\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n679\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n680\t        s.to_string()\n681\t    } else {\n682\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n683\t        format!(\"{}... section headers.\n690\t///\n691\t/// ## Example\n692\t///\n693\t/// ```\n694\t/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n695\t///\n696\t/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output combined.push('\\n');\n714\t        }\n715\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n716\t        combined.push_str(stderr);\n717\t        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n718\t            combined.push('\\n');\n719\t        }\n720\t    }\n721\t\n722\t    combined\n723\t}\n724\t\n725\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n726\t// Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n            } else {\n                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process with timeout handling\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n\n        // Use a thread to handle output() with timeout\n        let output_result = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            cmd.output()\n        });\n\n        // Wait for thread completion with timeout\n        let output = loop {\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                    exit_code: None,\n                    stdout: String::new(),\n                    stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                    duration: start.elapsed(),\n                    timed_out: true,\n                    compilation_failed: false,\n                    compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            // Check if thread is complete\n            if output_result.is_finished() {\n                match output_result.join() {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => break output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to execute cargo test: {}\", e))\n                            .with_context(|| \"failed to spawn or execute cargo test\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cargo test thread panicked\"));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n        };\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to bead trace directory.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout and stderr\n    /// to files in the `.beads/traces/<bead-id>/` directory. This is used to\n    /// record test execution output for debugging and analysis.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `bead_id` - The bead ID to use for the trace directory name\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Trace directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let bead_id = \"bf-12345\";\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_bead_trace(bead_id).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_bead_trace(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create bead trace directory and write outputs\n        let bead_id = BeadId::from(bead_id);\n        if let Some(trace) = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = trace.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to trace file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                trace_dir = %trace.trace_dir().display(),\n                stdout_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stdout.txt\").display(),\n                stderr_path = %trace.trace_dir().join(\"stderr.txt\").display(),\n                \"test output written to bead trace files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                \"failed to create bead trace directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n183\t\n184\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n185\t///\n186\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n187\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n188\tpub enum Outcome {\n189\t    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n190\t    Success,\n191\t    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n192\t    Failure,\n193\t    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n194\t    Timeout,\n195\t    /// Exit 126 code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n200\t    Crash(i32),\n201\t}\n202\t\n203\timpl Outcome {\n204\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n205\t    ///\n206\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n207\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n208\t    ///\n209\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n210\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n211\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n212\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n213\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n214\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n215\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n216\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n217\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n218\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n219\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n220\t        if was_interrupted {\n221\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n222\t        }\n223\t\n224\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n225\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n226\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n227\t        match exit_code {\n228\t            // Success\n229\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n230\t            // Explicit failure code\n231\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n232\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n233\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n234\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n235\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n236\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n237\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n238\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n239\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n240\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n241\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n242\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n243\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n244\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n245\t        }\n246\t    }\n247\t\n248\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n249\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n250\t        match self {\n251\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n252\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n253\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n254\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n255\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n256\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n257\t        }\n258\t    }\n259\t}\n260\t\n261\t// Usage\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use needle::trace::TraceCapture;\n//! use needle::types::BeadId;\n//! use std::path::Path;\n//!\n//! // Create trace capture for a bead\n//! let bead_id = BeadId::from(\"bf-12345\");\n//! let trace = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, Path::new(\".\")).unwrap();\n//!\n//! // Write trace outputs\n//! trace.write_stdout(\"Test stdout content\").unwrap();\n//! trace.write_stderr(\"Test stderr content\").unwrap();\n//! ```\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::types::BeadId;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Constants\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Bead directory name\npub const BEADS_DIR_NAME: &str = \".beads\";\n\n/// Traces subdirectory name\npub const TRACES_DIR_NAME: &str = \"traces\";\n\n/// Stdout output file name\npub const STDOUT_FILE: &str = \"stdout.txt\";\n\n/// Stderr output file name\npub const STDERR_FILE: &str = \"stderr.txt\";\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Trace capture management\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Manages trace output files for a single bead.\npub struct TraceCapture {\n    /// Trace directory for this bead (`.beads/traces/<bead-id>`).\n    trace_dir: PathBuf,\n    /// Whether trace capture is enabled.\n    enabled: bool,\n}\n\nimpl TraceCapture {\n    /// Create a new trace capture manager for a bead.\n    ///\n    /// `bead_id` is the bead identifier (e.g., \"bf-12345\").\n    /// `workspace_root` is the workspace root directory where `.beads/traces/` will be created.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the trace directory cannot be created.\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::trace::TraceCapture;\n    /// use needle::types::BeadId;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let bead_id = BeadId::from(\"bf-12345\");\n    /// let trace = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, Path::new(\".\")).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn new(bead_id: &BeadId, workspace_root: &Path) -> Option<Self> {\n        let trace_dir = workspace_root\n            .join(BEADS_DIR_NAME)\n            .join(TRACES_DIR_NAME)\n            .join(bead_id.as_ref());\n\n        // Create the trace directory with proper error handling\n        if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&trace_dir) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to create bead trace directory, trace capture disabled\"\n            );\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        Some(TraceCapture {\n            trace_dir,\n            enabled: true,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the trace directory path.\n    pub fn trace_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.trace_dir\n    }\n\n    /// Write stdout to `stdout.txt`.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - Trace capture is disabled\n    /// - File write operation fails\n    pub fn write_stderr(&self, stderr: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(STDERR_FILE);\n        std::fs::write(&path, stderr.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write trace stderr: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Get the stdout file path.\n    pub fn stdout_path(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.trace_dir.join(STDOUT_FILE)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the stderr file path.\n    pub fn stderr_path(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.trace_dir.join(STDERR_FILE)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if stdout file exists.\n    pub fn has_stdout(&self) -> bool {\n        self.stdout_path().exists()\n    }\n\n    /// Check if stderr file exists.\n    pub fn has_stderr(&self) -> bool {\n        self.stderr_path().exists()\n    }\n\n    /// Read stdout content if it exists.\n    pub fn read_stdout(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        std::fs::read_to_string(self.stdout_path()).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to read trace stdout: {}\",\n                self.stdout_path().display()\n            )\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read stderr content if it exists.\n    pub fn read_stderr(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        std::fs::read_to_string(self.stderr_path()).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to read trace stderr: {}\",\n                self.stderr_path().display()\n            )\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Delete all trace files and the directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::trace::TraceCapture;\n    /// use needle::types::BeadId;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let bead_id = BeadId::from(\"bf-12345\");\n    /// let trace = TraceCapture::new(&bead_id, Path::new(\".\")).unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn new(bead_id: &BeadId, workspace_root: &Path) -> Option<Self> {\n        let trace_dir = workspace_root\n            .join(BEADS_DIR_NAME)\n            .join(TRACES_DIR_NAME)\n            .join(bead_id.as_ref());\n\n        // Create the trace directory with proper error handling\n        if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&trace_dir) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead_id,\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to create bead trace directory, trace capture disabled\"\n            );\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        Some(TraceCapture {\n            trace_dir,\n            enabled: true,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the trace directory path.\n    pub fn trace_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.trace_dir\n    }\n\n    /// Write stdout to `stdout.txt`.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - Trace capture is disabled\n    /// - File write operation fails\n    pub fn write_stdout(&self, stdout: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.enabled {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let path = self.trace_dir.join(STDOUT_FILE);\n        std::fs::write(&path, stdout.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write trace stdout: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Write stderr to `stderr.txt`.\n    ///\n    /// ## only\n293\tpub fn cleanup_traces(\n294\t    traces_dir: &Path,\n295\t    retention_days_failed: u32,\n296\t    retention_days_success: u32,\n297\t) -> Result<TraceCleanupSummary> {\n298\t    let mut summary = TraceCleanupSummary::default();\n299\t\n300\t    if !traces_dir.exists() {\n301\t        return Ok(summary);\n302\t    }\n303\t\n304\t    let now = SystemTime::now()\n305\t        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n306\t        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n307\t        .unwrap_or(0);\n308\t\n309\t    // Iterate through bead trace directories.\n310\t    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(traces_dir)\n311\t        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read traces directory: {}\", traces_dir.display()))?\n312\t    {\n313\t        let entry = match entry {\n314\t            Ok(e) => e,\n315\t            Err(_) => continue,\n316\t        };\n317\t\n318\t        let path = entry.path();\n319\t\n320\t        // Only process directories (bead-id subdirectories).\n321\t        if !path.is_dir() {\n322\t            continue;\n323\t        }\n324\t\n325\t        // Check metadata.json to determine outcome and age.\n326\t        let metadata_path = path.join(\"metadata.json\");\n327\t        let metadata: Option<TraceMetadata> = metadata_path\n328\t            .exists()\n329\t            .then(|| {\n330\t                let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path).ok()?;\n331\t                serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()\n332\t            })\n333\t            .flatten();\n334\t\n335\t        let age_days = metadata\n336\t            .as_ref()\n337\t            .and_then(|m| now.checked_sub(m.captured_at.timestamp() as u64))\n338\t            .map(|secs| secs / 86400)\n339\t            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n340\t\n341\t        let is_failed = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.exit_code != 0).unwrap_or(false);\n342\t        let is_pruned = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.pruned).unwrap_or(false);\n343\t\n344\t        // Check if trace data files actually exist before attempting to prune.\n345\t        // This prevents counting a trace as \"pruned\" when the data files were\n346\t        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n347\t        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n348\t        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n349\t        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"]\n350\t            .iter()\n351\t            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n352\t\n353\t        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n354\t        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n355\t        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n356\t        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n357\t        let should_prune =\n358\t            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n359\t\n360\t        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n361\t        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n362\t        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n363\t            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n364\t                tracing::debug!(\n365\t                    path = %path.display(),\n366\t                    error = %e,\n367\t                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n368\t                );\n369\t            }\n370\t        }\n371\t\n372\t        if should_delete {\n373\t            // Delete entire trace directory.\n374\t            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n375\t                tracing::warn!(\n376\t                    path = %path.display(),\n377\t                    error = %e,\n378\t                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n379\t                );\n380\t            } else {\n381\t                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n382\t            }\n383\t        } else if should_prune {\n384\t            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n385\t            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n386\t                tracing::warn!(\n387\t                    path = %path.display(),\n388\t                    error = %e,\n389\t                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n390\t                );\n391\t            } else {\n392\t                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n393\t            }\n394\t        }\n395\t    }\n396\t\n397\t    Ok(summary)\n398\t}\n399\t\n400\t/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n401\t/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\n402\tfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n403\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n404\t    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n405\t        return Ok(());\n406\t    }\n407\t\n408\t    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n409\t    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n410\t        if !metadata.pruned {\n411\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n412\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n413\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n414\t            tracing::debug!(\n415\t                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n416\t                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n417\t            );\n418\t        }\n419\t    }\n420\t    Ok(())\n421\t}\n422\t\n423\t/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n424\t///\n425\t/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n426\t/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n427\t/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n428\t/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n429\t/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\n430\tfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n431\t    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n432\t    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n433\t    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n434\t    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n435\t    if metadata_path.exists() {\n436\t        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n437\t        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n438\t            metadata.pruned = true;\n439\t            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n440\t            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n441\t        }\n442\t    }\n443\t\n444\t    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n445\t    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n446\t    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n447\t    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"] {\n448\t        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n449\t        if path.exists() {\n450\t            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n451\t                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n452\t        }\n453\t    }\n454\t\n455\t    Ok(())\n456\t}\n457\t\n458\tuse std::time::SystemTime;\n459\t\n460\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n461\t// Tests\n462\t// - Failed beads (non-zero exit): delete after 30 days\n/// - Successful beads (exit 0): prune data after 7 days, keep metadata only\npub fn cleanup_traces(\n    traces_dir: &Path,\n    retention_days_failed: u32,\n    retention_days_success: u32,\n) -> Result<TraceCleanupSummary> {\n    let mut summary = TraceCleanupSummary::default();\n\n    if !traces_dir.exists() {\n        return Ok(summary);\n    }\n\n    let now = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n\n    // Iterate through bead trace directories.\n    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(traces_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read traces directory: {}\", traces_dir.display()))?\n    {\n        let entry = match entry {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(_) => continue,\n        };\n\n        let path = entry.path();\n\n        // Only process directories (bead-id subdirectories).\n        if !path.is_dir() {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check metadata.json to determine outcome and age.\n        let metadata_path = path.join(\"metadata.json\");\n        let metadata: Option<TraceMetadata> = metadata_path\n            .exists()\n            .then(|| {\n                let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path).ok()?;\n                serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()\n            })\n            .flatten();\n\n        let age_days = metadata\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|m| now.checked_sub(m.captured_at.timestamp() as u64))\n            .map(|secs| secs / 86400)\n            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n\n        let is_failed = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.exit_code != 0).unwrap_or(false);\n        let is_pruned = metadata.as_ref().map(|m| m.pruned).unwrap_or(false);\n\n        // Check if trace data files actually exist before attempting to prune.\n        // This prevents counting a trace as \"pruned\" when the data files were\n        // already removed in a previous run but the metadata update failed\n        // or was interrupted. This check is crucial for preventing infinite\n        // loops where the same trace is counted repeatedly.\n        let has_data_files = [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"]\n            .iter()\n            .any(|file| path.join(file).exists());\n\n        let should_delete = is_failed && age_days > retention_days_failed as u64;\n        // Only prune if metadata says not pruned AND data files actually exist.\n        // If files are gone but metadata says not pruned, we have a partial\n        // state from an interrupted run - fix the metadata and skip counting.\n        let should_prune =\n            !is_failed && !is_pruned && has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64;\n\n        // Fix up metadata for traces that were partially pruned (files gone\n        // but metadata not updated). This prevents infinite loops.\n        if !is_failed && !is_pruned && !has_data_files && age_days > retention_days_success as u64 {\n            if let Err(e) = fix_pruned_metadata(&path) {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to fix pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        if should_delete {\n            // Delete entire trace directory.\n            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to delete old trace directory\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_deleted += 1;\n            }\n        } else if should_prune {\n            // Prune trace data, keep metadata.\n            if let Err(e) = prune_trace_dir(&path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to prune trace data\"\n                );\n            } else {\n                summary.traces_pruned += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(summary)\n}\n\n/// Fix metadata for a trace that was partially pruned (data files gone but\n/// metadata not updated). This is a recovery operation for interrupted pruning.\nfn fix_pruned_metadata(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if !metadata_path.exists() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n    if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n        if !metadata.pruned {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n            tracing::debug!(\n                path = %trace_dir.display(),\n                \"fixed pruned metadata for partially-pruned trace\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Prune trace data files in a directory, keeping only metadata.json.\n///\n/// Updates metadata FIRST to mark as pruned, then removes data files.\n/// This order is critical: if the process is interrupted after metadata\n/// update but before file removal, the next cleanup will skip this trace\n/// (because is_pruned=true) and only remove remaining files. This prevents\n/// infinite loops where the same traces are counted as \"pruned\" repeatedly.\nfn prune_trace_dir(trace_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    // Step 1: Update metadata to mark as pruned BEFORE removing files.\n    // This prevents the same trace from being counted as pruned multiple times\n    // if the process is interrupted between metadata update and file removal.\n    let metadata_path = trace_dir.join(\"metadata.json\");\n    if metadata_path.exists() {\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&metadata_path)?;\n        if let Ok(mut metadata) = serde_json::from_str::<TraceMetadata>(&content) {\n            metadata.pruned = true;\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metadata)?;\n            std::fs::write(&metadata_path, json)?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Step 2: Remove trace data files after metadata is updated.\n    // Use ? to propagate errors - if file removal fails, the operator should\n    // know so they can investigate. Files that don't exist are skipped.\n    for file in [\"trace.jsonl\", \"stdout.txt\", \"stderr.txt\"] {\n        let path = trace_dir.join(file);\n        if path.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&path)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to prune trace file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nuse std::time::SystemTime;\n\n//
